title: Edge SDKenV smoke & probe notebook
content:
Purpose:
A compact, hands-on notebook for the SDK "edge" developer environment (local / constrained-network / ephemeral VM) focused on three things: quick smoke checks, micro-telemetry probes (latency, token-cost, cache-hit), and lightweight safety heuristics for prompt flows. This lives as an iterative lab doc for new SDK changes and partner integrators to run in ~15–30 minutes.

Background / motivation:
- We keep seeing non-reproducible first-run flakiness across mac/linux dev machines and CI sandboxes tied to warm-up behavior (KV cache priming, tokenizer coldstarts, kernel selection to quantized runtime).
- Need a tiny, consistent checklist that devs (and SEs) can run before filing a bug or escalating to infra.
- Make telemetry minimal and actionable so early experiments show whether regressions are infra/runtime/model or integration-level.

Structure of the notebook (3 quick labs):
1) 5–10min smoke (sanity)
   - Goal: confirm basic SDK surface + auth + endpoint reachability.
   - Steps:
     1. Export a short-lived token (use auth helper): export REDWOOD_TOKEN=test-token-XXXX
     2. Curl generation (single-shot):
        curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
          -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" 
          -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
          -d '{"model":"redwood-mini-1","input":"Say hi to the dev team used for smoke tests"}'
     3. Check: HTTP 200, response.tokens_generated > 0, first token latency < 600ms (local-on-VM tolerance).
   - Quick probes to capture: RTT, HTTP status, tokens_out, error_code (if present).

2) 15min warmstart + cache sanity
   - Goal: observe cache/KV warmstart behavior and per-token cost slope.
   - Flow:
     a) Send a short repeated prompt sequence (3 requests of identical prefix, then 3 longer sequences) to surface prefix caching behavior.
     b) Measure tokens_per_request and per_token_latency over the run.
     c) Verify that token-latency improves on repeated prefix (~>15–40% improvement) or that cache-hit metric is being emitted.
   - Commands (node/python snippet allowed): run a small loop hitting the same conversation id and log X-Trace-ID header.
   - Expected micro-telemetry keys to surface: "rdw.cache.hit_ratio", "rdw.kv.prime_ms", "rdw.token.lat_p50", "rdw.token.lat_p95", "rdw.cost.estimated_per_1000".
   - Acceptance: either cache hit ratio >= 0.2 for repeated prefixes OR explicit note that the runtime is configured quantized-no-cache (explicit config).

3) 20–30min offline / flaky-network resilience lab
   - Goal: validate local fallback, offline-stub behavior, and deterministic error messaging for network partitions.
   - Steps:
     1. Start a local stub server (small stub that returns 503 or throttled responses).
     2. Ensure SDK fallback to cached response when offline and circuit-breaker behavior when sustained 5xxs.
     3. Validate that telemetry contains "rdw.fallback.used" and has the reason code.
   - Check items: clear messaging in SDK logs, reproducible retry timings, test hooks to simulate slow kernels.

Micro-telemetry: minimum set (what to emit from SDK runtime/client during these labs)
- Request-level: rdw.request.id, rdw.request.mode (stream|sync|embed), rdw.model.name, rdw.route.tier
- Latency: rdw.latency.total_ms, rdw.latency.server_ms, rdw.latency.token_p50_ms, rdw.latency.token_p95_ms
- Cost: rdw.tokens.in, rdw.tokens.out, rdw.cost.estimate_per_1k_tokens
- Cache: rdw.cache.hit, rdw.cache.hitrate_window_1m
- Resilience: rdw.fallback.used, rdw.fallback.reason, rdw.retry.attempts
- Errors: rdw.error.class, rdw.error.code, rdw.error.message (short)

Minimal alert thresholds (dev sandbox) - suggested, tweak per infra:
- request.latency.p95 > 2000ms for 5+ requests in 1m -> warn (telemetry trace)
- rdw.cache.hitrate_window_1m < 0.05 for repeated-prefix workload -> investigation
- rdw.fallback.used == true and fallback.reason == "capacity" -> open infra ticket

Lightweight safety heuristics to run locally (dev-level):
- Prompt size guard: warn when prompt_tokens + expected_output_tokens > 12k (configurable).
- Unsafe token detection: flag when model generates any token matching the local PII regex sample: (email|SSN-like patterns) and surface in rdw.error.safety_flag (do not persist content, only boolean and reason).
- Quick check: run a short test prompt with user-provided sample and ensure the SDK returns structured safety flag if triggered.

Developer checklist (one-pager to run before filing a bug):
- [ ] Confirm latest SDK binary (git rev + build stamp) and platform (darwin/linux).
- [ ] Run smoke lab -> HTTP 200, tokens_generated > 0
- [ ] Run warmstart loop, record rdw.cache.hitrate_window_1m and token latencies
- [ ] Simulate flaky network, validate fallback flags and clear error reason codes
- [ ] Check telemetry trace uploaded (or local-file if offline) and attach rdw.request.id in bug report
- [ ] Paste minimal reproducible script (<= 30 lines) to reproduce in ticket

Quick how-to: capture a trace for PRs/bug reports
1) Export: export RDW_TRACE=on; export RDW_OUTPUT=./rdw-trace.json
2) Rerun the failing sequence (include RDW_TRACE header)
3) Attach rdw-trace.json to the issue. In the trace include: request id, start/end timestamps, key metrics, and a short human note describing expected vs observed.

Open questions / discussion points (work in progress):
- Do we push full token-level timings in dev traces or only aggregated p50/p95? (privacy + size tradeoff)
- Should the default dev telemetry redact prompt text by default? (prefers boolean safety flags only)
- How to make cache-warmup deterministic for integration tests (seeded prompt fixtures?)
- Aligning local SDK retry logic with Dedicated autoscaling fallbacks vs. Hosted API semantics.

Next steps / owners:
- Priya: prototype trace capture CLI helper (rdw-trace init) -> due 2026-02-20
- Leo: add minimal telemetry keys to SDK client (emit for smoke & warmstart) -> PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 (WIP) -> due 2026-02-14
- Maya: create a short internal demo (5–10min recording) showing the 3 labs for SEs and Solutions Eng -> due 2026-02-28

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Keep the notebook short: target 1 page printable "dev preflight checklist"
- When adding sample config, include explicit flags: --no-cache, --trace, --offline-stub
- Consider a tiny GH action that runs the smoke lab on PR changes to client/telemetry code (should be hermetic).

References and links:
- proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412
- infra ticket: JIRA:INF-4123 (runtime telemetry)
- design doc stub: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEVEXP/pages/12345

Quick copy-paste sample (python) for the smoke test (<=20 lines):
```
import os, requests
TOK=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_TOKEN')
url='https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
body={'model':'redwood-mini-1','input':'smoke run: hello'}
r=requests.post(url,headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer {TOK}'},json=body,timeout=10)
print('status',r.status_code,'len',len(r.text))
print('headers',r.headers.get('X-Rdw-Req-Id'))
```
If anything is unclear ping #devexp or drop a quick Loom to the thread. This is intentionally terse — we want something people actually run while diagnosing first-run flakiness.

-- Maya
